blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Embodied world models predict the visual consequences of candidate actions before execution. However, existing action-conditioned world models often adopt uniformly weighted visual generation objectives that can be misaligned with embodied prediction needs. Even with explicit motion conditioning, these objectives can underemphasize spatially sparse changes that are critical to interaction.
We propose K i n e W o rld , a transport-aware world-modeling framework that extends robot kinematics from motion conditioning to the spatial allocation of generative supervision. Kinematic Transport Lifting (KTL) constructs renderer-derived, camera-aligned transport fields from commanded robot motion. Transport-Aware World Diffusion (TAWD) calibrates their motion support on the video-latent grid and reweights future-RGB flow matching through a normalized mixture of uniform and transport-focused distributions.
We train KineWorld using ALOHA–AgileX bimanual manipulation data from RoboTwin 2.0 . KineWorld achieves an EWMScore-P of 68.95 in single-view evaluation and a TWB-Score of 54.82 in multi-view evaluation. These results support a shift from appearance fitting toward action-consequence modeling for embodied decision-making.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: World Action Models (WAMs) enable robots to anticipate how the visual world will evolve under candidate actions before executing them in the physical environment. By generating action-conditioned future observations, these models can serve as predictive simulators for policy learning, action evaluation, planning, and synthetic experience generation. Recent advances in large-scale video generation further provide strong appearance and dynamics priors, making it possible to construct visually realistic robot rollouts from limited embodied data Zhu et al. (2024) ; Guo et al. (2025) ; Liao et al. (2025) .
blocks.zh: 世界行动模式(WAMS)使机器人在实际环境中执行前能够预见到在候选行动下视觉世界将如何演变. 这些模型通过生成有行动条件的未来观测结果,可以作为政策学习、行动评价、规划和合成经验生成的预测模拟器。 近期在大规模视频生成方面的进步进一步提供了强烈的外观和动态前传,使得能够从有限的包含数据朱等(2024年);郭等(2025年);廖等(2025年)构建出视觉现实的机器人推出.

blocks.en:
Existing world action models (WAMs) improve action responsiveness through numerical action tokens, learned latent codes, and spatially aligned conditions such as embodiment masks, action images, optical flow, and projected kinematic fields Zhu et al. (2024) ; Guo et al. (2025) ; Wang et al. (2026) ; Liao et al. (2025) ; Chen et al. (2026b) . Yet motion conditioning does not itself alter the spatial weighting of the primary RGB-generation objective. When action-responsive regions occupy only a small part of the frame, uniform token averaging can bias optimization toward static appearance. Motion-sensitive auxiliary objectives and flow-branch reweighting address related concerns Zhu et al. (2024) ; Chen et al. (2026b) . We further use robot kinematics to guide future-RGB supervision, aligning the model’s learning priorities with action consequences.
This raises a key question: how can robot kinematics guide the learning of action consequences?

blocks.en:
Our key insight is that action conditioning and supervision allocation serve different purposes: the former specifies what motion to generate, whereas the latter determines which prediction errors receive greater weight during training. Robot kinematics provides a geometry-derived prior for this allocation by identifying where commanded robot motion is expected to appear in the camera view, without relying on generated future frames. This suggests using kinematic transport not only as a generation condition, but also as a spatial prior for the primary
video-generation objective.

视频生成目标。

blocks.en:
Building on this insight, we introduce K i n e W o rld , a
transport-aware training framework for action-conditioned world modeling. Kinematic Transport Lifting (KTL) constructs camera-aligned transport, while Transport-Aware World Diffusion (TAWD) calibrates its motion support on the video latent grid and converts the resulting support into a normalized mixture distribution for the RGB flow-matching objective. The resulting objective redistributes supervision while preserving the aggregate token weight, without adding inference parameters or sampling steps. This extends kinematic priors from generation conditions to learning guidance for interaction- and decision-oriented world prediction.
Our main contributions are summarized as follows: • Action-Consequence-Oriented Learning. We distinguish visual extent from interaction importance, motivating
kinematics-guided learning of interaction-critical local changes. • K i n e W o rld Framework. We propose K i n e W o rld , a transport-aware framework with KTL and TAWD. KTL constructs camera-aligned transport from the commanded rollout, while TAWD reweights RGB flow matching via a normalized mixture on the latent grid, preserving token weight and sampling. • Benchmark Evaluation. Trained on RoboTwin 2.0 ALOHA–AgileX bimanual manipulation data ( Chen et al., 2025 ) , KineWorld achieves an EWMScore-P of 68.95 and a TWB-Score of 54.82 in single-view and multi-view evaluation, respectively. Our framework and evaluations provide the community with a reference for action-consequence-oriented world modeling.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: World Action Models (WAMs) increasingly leverage pretrained video generators to connect visual prediction with robot control ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Liao et al., 2025 ) . Existing approaches include action-conditioned video prediction ( Zhu et al., 2024 ; Guo et al., 2025 ) , joint video-action generation ( Zhou et al., 2026 ) , and action decoding from visual latent representations ( Liao et al., 2025 ) . Recent systems further broaden this paradigm. RealWonder connects physical actions to video generation through simulated RGB and flow ( Liu et al., 2026 ) , while CLAP integrates heterogeneous action representations for cross-embodiment learning ( Liu & Shorinwa, 2026 ) . However, advances in generative architectures and action interfaces do not inherently prioritize interaction-critical changes in the primary RGB objective. When these changes occupy few visual tokens, uniform weighting can underemphasize their contribution. KineWorld addresses this complementary problem through kinematics-guided allocation of future-RGB supervision.

KineWorld通过以动能指导方式分配未来-RGB监督,解决了这个互补的问题.

blocks.en: Existing WAMs encode robot actions as numerical tokens, learned latent codes, or spatially grounded visual cues ( Zhu et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2026a ; Zhou et al., 2026 ) . Recent methods align actions with the visual domain through embodiment masks ( Chen et al., 2026c ) , multi-view action videos ( Zhen et al., 2026 ) , optical flow ( Chen et al., 2026b ) , and camera-aligned kinematic fields ( Yang et al., 2026 ) . Beyond conditioning, FlowWAM reweights its flow-branch loss using reference-relative latent deviations ( Chen et al., 2026b ) , while EA-WM uses frame-difference supervision to guide cross-stream fusion ( Yang et al., 2026 ) . In contrast, KineWorld uses kinematic transport to directly reweight future-RGB flow matching without introducing auxiliary objectives.

blocks.en: 4.1 Overview
blocks.zh: 4.1 概览

blocks.en:
KineWorld is a latent video world model that predicts future RGB observations from the current observation, a language instruction, and a candidate action sequence. A causal video VAE represents visual states in latent space, while a conditional flow model learns their action-conditioned dynamics. When projected robot motion occupies only a small part of the video, uniform token averaging assigns this region a correspondingly small share of the total token weight. KineWorld uses commanded kinematics to guide both generation and learning: camera-aligned transport conditions the predicted motion, while its spatial support directs a fixed share of future-RGB supervision toward regions of projected robot motion. KineWorld comprises two components. Kinematic Transport Lifting
(KTL) constructs camera-aligned transport and injects its latent representation z u z^{u} into the video generator as a clean structural condition. Transport-Aware World Diffusion (TAWD) derives calibrated support d d from the transport fields and constructs normalized token weights for the
flow-matching objective. KTL supplies motion conditions during both training
and inference, whereas TAWD modifies only training-time supervision.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: We presented KineWorld, a kinematics-guided framework for action-conditioned video prediction. KTL constructs camera-aligned transport, and TAWD calibrates its support and uses it to redistribute future-RGB supervision between action-responsive regions and the full scene. The objective preserves the total token weight and recovers uniform supervision under zero motion, without adding inference parameters or denoising steps. Trained on ALOHA–AgileX bimanual manipulation data from RoboTwin 2.0 , KineWorld achieves an EWMScore-P of 68.95 in single-view evaluation and a TWB-Score of 54.82 in multi-view evaluation. These results highlight the potential of kinematics-guided supervision to advance world models from appearance fitting toward action-consequence modeling for embodied decision-making.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了KineWorld, 一个动能指导框架 行动条件的视频预测。 KTL构建相机相接运输,TAWD校正其支持,并用它来重新分配未来-RGB在行动响应地区和全场之间的监督. 目标保留了总的象征重量并恢复了零运动下的统一监督,而不增加推论参数或去名步骤. 在ALOHA-Agile上受训 来自RoboTwin 2.0的X双人操控数据,KineWorld在单景评价中实现了68.95的EWMScore-P,在多景评价中实现了54.82的TWB-Score. 这些成果突出表明了以动能为指导的监督将世界模型从外观上推向为体现的决策制定行动-后果模型的潜力。

blocks.en: KineWorld relies on calibrated robot and camera models, and its transport support does not explicitly capture object motion or contact dynamics. Future work will investigate calibration-robust transport estimation, object-aware supervision, and contact-aware world modeling.
blocks.zh: KineWorld依赖于被校准的机器人和相机模型,其运输支持并没有明确地捕捉物体运动或接触动力学. 今后的工作将调查校正-活性运输估计、物体意识监督和接触意识世界建模。

blocks.en: A.1 Broader Impacts
blocks.zh: A.1 更广泛的影响

blocks.en: KineWorld may improve the action responsiveness of embodied world models by directing learning toward image regions that are causally associated with commanded robot motion. More faithful action-conditioned rollouts could support simulation, policy evaluation, and data generation while reducing unnecessary physical interaction. At the same time, generated videos remain predictions rather than certified physical trajectories: errors in calibration, contact modeling, or long-horizon generation can produce plausible but unsafe outcomes. KineWorld should therefore be used together with independent feasibility checks, collision detection, controller limits, and validation on the target robot.
blocks.zh: KineWorld可能通过将学习引导到与受命机器人运动因果相关的图像区域来提高所体现世界模型的动作响应能力. 更加忠实的行动有条件的推出可以支持模拟、政策评价和数据生成,同时减少不必要的物理互动。 与此同时,生成的视频仍然是预测而不是经过认证的物理轨迹:校准、接触模型或长视距生成中的错误可以产生可信但不安全的结果。 因此,KineWorld应与独立的可行性检查、碰撞探测、控制器限制和对目标机器人的验证一起使用。

blocks.en: A.2 Contributions
blocks.zh: A.2 缴款

blocks.en: We distinguish action conditioning from supervision allocation. Action-induced motion can occupy only a small fraction of video-latent tokens, so uniform averaging of the RGB-generation objective can underemphasize prediction errors in action-responsive regions. Explicit motion conditions alone do not correct this weighting imbalance.
blocks.zh: 我们区分行动条件和监管分配。 由行动引起的运动只能占据一小部分视频相向信号,因此RGB生成目标的统一平均值可以低估行动反应区域的预测错误. 仅凭明确的运动条件并不能纠正这种加权不平衡。

blocks.en: We introduce KineWorld, a transport-aware embodied world-modeling framework that promotes robot kinematics from an auxiliary condition to a signal for allocating generative supervision. Given the initial embodiment configuration and commanded action sequence, KineWorld constructs camera-aligned transport support and redistributes token-wise supervision between global scene modeling and action-responsive regions while preserving the total token weight.
blocks.zh: 我们介绍KineWorld, 一个包含着世界模型的交通意识框架, 它促进机器人动能 从辅助条件到分配基因监督的信号。 鉴于最初的布局和指挥动作序列,KineWorld构建相机相接的运输支持,并重新分配全球场景模型制作与行动反应区域之间的象征性监督,同时保留了总的象征性重量。

blocks.en: Kinematic Transport Lifting (KTL) rolls out the commanded configurations, renders the embodiment from the observation camera, and estimates source-supported inter-frame transport. Transport-Aware World Diffusion (TAWD) calibrates this activity on the video-latent grid, converts the calibrated support into a normalized mixture distribution, and uses mean-one weights to reallocate the conditional flow-matching objective, while preserving uniform supervision under zero motion and introducing no additional denoising steps.
blocks.zh: Kinematic Transport Lefting (KTL) 推出指令配置,使从观测相机中化为浮出水面,并估算出源支持的相机间传输. Transport-Award World Difusion(TAWD)在视频相位网格上校正了这一活性,将校正后支持转换为规范的混合物配给,并使用正一权重来再分配有条件的流量配比目标,同时在零运动下保持统一监督,并不再引入额外的去诺步骤.

blocks.en: Our evaluation distinguishes retained system profiles, local generation diagnostics, and an executed matched comparison. In the matched comparison, two 50-update continuations start from the same step-315 checkpoint, keep KTL conditioning fixed, and differ only in the future-RGB weighting parameter β \beta . Changing β = 0 \beta=0 to β = 1 \beta=1 improves EWMScore-P from 66.10 to 67.85 ( Δ = + 1.75 \Delta=+1.75 ), with additional gains of 5.60 points in Trajectory Accuracy and 4.20 points in Interaction Quality.
blocks.zh: 我们的评价区分了所保留的系统概况、本地生成诊断和已执行的匹配比较。 在相匹配的比较中,两个50更新的续作从同步-315的检查站起步,保持KTL调节固定,并且只在未来的-RGB加权参数β\beta中有所区别. 将β=0\β=0改为β=1\β=1改进了EWMScore-P由66.10改为67.85(Δ=+1.75\德尔塔+1.75=1.75),在轨迹精确度上再增加5.60分,在相互作用质量上增加4.20分.

blocks.en: The three-view protocol uses synchronized head, left-wrist, and right-wrist observations together with an initial robot state, instruction, and action sequence. Each view uses its own camera calibration and transport condition, including time-dependent extrinsics for moving wrist cameras. The reported inference convention generates 17 uniformly spaced keyframes and expands them to the episode length. This convention describes temporal sampling and does not define episode membership. Reference-based metrics use the corresponding future observations from each camera.

blocks.en: The appendix separates four evidence layers: externally reported system profiles, the retained KineWorld candidate profile, local generation diagnostics, and the executed matched TAWD comparison in Table 7 . The first three layers retain their original evaluation scope and do not provide common-training causal estimates. The matched comparison fixes initialization, training budget, KTL conditioning, data order, and evaluation, and changes only β \beta . The retained KineWorld profile has EWMScore-P 68.95, whereas the matched β = 1 \beta=1 continuation in Table 7 has EWMScore-P 67.85. These values correspond to different training scopes and are not intended as two measurements of the same run. EWMScore-P follows the 15-component perceptual scoring convention defined in Appendix A.3.1 ; TWB-Score follows TriWorldBench’s separate 19-component multi-view convention in Appendix A.3.2 . Neither is a newly proposed metric or a RoboTwin 2.0 task success rate. Method citations identify the underlying approaches; they do not establish common evaluation conditions. blocks.en: The transport field is a renderer-derived, camera-aligned estimate of projected robot motion, not a sufficient statistic for the full action. Gripper semantics, contact forces, object state, and unobserved dynamics may not be recoverable from image-plane transport alone. KineWorld uses this estimate to decide where supervision is concentrated while language, the initial scene, and the generative model retain responsibility for the remaining dynamics. blocks.en: We count instantiated denoiser tensor entries rather than checkpoint bytes and identify trainable parameters from the frozen continuation contract. The Wan2.2 DiT contains 4,999,787,712 parameters. The transport input/output stream adds 1,192,128 parameters, or 0.02384% of the DiT, for an active single-view denoising path of 5,000,979,840 parameters (100.02384% of the DiT). TAWD is a training objective and therefore adds zero learned parameters. The selected self-attention-LoRA continuation exposes 80,415,936 trainable parameters (1.60839% of the DiT): 67,430,400 modulation parameters, 11,796,480 LoRA parameters, and 1,189,056 parameters in the checkpoint-version transport stream. The 3,072-parameter difference between this training contract and the instantiated inference stream is the inference revision’s stream-identity embedding; rounding both footprints to two decimal places gives 1.19M transport and 80.42M trainable parameters. This trainable subset is not an additional component to be added to the denoiser total. An optional 778,125,326-parameter action expert (15.56317% of the DiT) is stored in the joint training checkpoint, but the reported single-view loader ignores it; we consequently exclude it from the active denoiser size. The frozen video VAE and text encoder are also excluded so that the count follows the DiT-backbone convention.

blocks.en: The measurements in Table A.6 are complementary local diagnostics rather than newly proposed or official benchmark metrics. Let Y t ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] H × W Y_{t}\in[0,1]^{H\times W} denote the luma channel of frame t t . A ​ - ​ MAD \operatorname{A\mbox{-}MAD} averages the pixel-wise absolute difference between adjacent Y t Y_{t} ; CPF \operatorname{CPF} reports the fraction of pixels whose adjacent-frame change exceeds the evaluator’s fixed threshold; and FL ​ - ​ MAD \operatorname{FL\mbox{-}MAD} applies the same absolute-difference statistic to the first and last frames. NDP \operatorname{NDP} is the fraction of adjacent pairs classified as near duplicates by a fixed frame-difference test. Frame differencing and cross-frame mean absolute differences have long been used in video analysis, including temporal-flicker evaluation ( Huang et al., 2024 ) .
blocks.zh: 表A.6中的衡量标准是补充性的当地诊断,而不是新提出的或正式的基准衡量标准。 让 Y t \ [0, 1] H \ W \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ 时间 W}表示帧 t 的 luma 通道。 A - MAD\ operatorname{A\ mbox{} MAD} 平均值相邻 Y t\\ t} 之间的像素绝对差; CPF\ operatorname{ CPF} 报告相邻帧变化超过评估者固定阈值的像素分数; FL - MAD\ operatorname{FL\ mbox{} } MAD} 对第一个和最后一个帧应用相同的绝对偏差统计 。 NDP\peratorname{ NDP} 是被固定帧偏差测试归类为近相重复的相邻对数的分数. 长期以来,在视频分析中使用了不同框架和跨框架的平均绝对差异,包括时间-闪克评估(Huang等人,2024年)。

blocks.en: For motion diagnostics, we estimate dense flow between adjacent frames with Farnebäck’s two-frame method ( Farnebäck, 2003 ) . FB ​ Mean \operatorname{FB\ Mean} and FB ​ P95 \operatorname{FB\ P95} are the mean and 95th percentile of the resulting flow magnitudes, while Jerk \operatorname{Jerk} summarizes temporal variation across successive flow fields as a heuristic smoothness measure. Related differential-flow and jerk-based analyses precede this work ( Shen et al., 2020 ; Takeda et al., 2018 ) . These statistics characterize different failure modes: adjacent differences are sensitive to both motion and flicker, first-to-last difference measures endpoint change but not path quality, near-duplicate rate exposes repetition, and flow magnitude or jerk does not by itself establish correct action-conditioned motion. We therefore assign no universal optimization direction and use the diagnostics only to interpret the interpolation ablation.
blocks.zh: 关于运动诊断,我们用法恩贝克的双帧方法估算相邻框架之间的密集流量(法恩贝克,2003年)。 FB 平均\operatorname{FB\Mean} 和 FB P95\operatorname{FB\P95} 是所产生的流度的平均值和第九十五分之一,而 Jerk\operatorname{Jerk} 则总结了相继流出字段的时间变化,作为热平滑度测量. 在这项工作之前,还进行了相关的差分流和混蛋分析(Shen等人,2020年;Takeda等人,2018年)。 这些统计对不同的故障模式具有特征:相邻差异对运动和闪烁器都敏感,先到最后的差别度量端点变化而不是路径质量,相近的重复率暴露出重复,而流度或混蛋本身并不建立正确的有行动条件的运动. 因此,我们没有指定通用优化方向,而只利用诊断来解释插值衰减。

blocks.en: A.10 Limitations and Reproducibility
blocks.zh: A.10 限制和可复制性

blocks.en: KineWorld relies on calibrated robot and camera models, and its transport support is sensitive to calibration errors, flow estimation errors, and occlusion. The support captures projected robot motion but does not explicitly model object motion or contact dynamics. Autoregressive rollout may accumulate appearance drift, while transport-focused supervision may trade visual fidelity for motion quality. The matched study evaluates TAWD over a 50-update continuation from a shared checkpoint; convergence and stability across training seeds remain to be assessed. Future work will investigate object-aware transport, calibration-robust conditioning, and cross-embodiment transfer.
blocks.zh: KineWorld依赖于被校正的机器人和相机模型,其运输支持对校正出错,流量估计出错,以及被隔离等敏感. 支持能捕捉到所预测的机器人运动,但没有明确模拟物体运动或接触动力学. 自动推出可能会累积外观漂移,而以运输为重点的监督则可能以视觉上的忠诚来换取运动的质量。 相应的研究评价TAWD通过共用检查站持续50个更新;培训种子的趋同和稳定性仍有待评估。 今后的工作将调查物体感知的运输、校准-活性调节和交叉活性转移。

blocks.en: Generated rollouts are predictive media rather than certified robot trajectories. They must not be used as evidence of collision-free or hardware-safe execution. Deployment requires independent state estimation, feasibility and collision checking, controller limits, emergency handling, and validation in the target simulator and robot system.
blocks.zh: 生成的推出是预测媒体,而不是经过认证的机器人轨迹. 不得将其作为无相撞或硬件安全执行的证据。 部署需要独立的状态估计,可行性和碰撞检查,控制器限制,紧急处理,以及目标模拟器和机器人系统的验证.

blocks.en: Reproducing the controlled comparison requires: • source code for rendering, support construction, training, sampling, and evaluation; • pinned environment and dependency versions, including renderer, RAFT, and VAE revisions; • data-split and episode manifests with checksums and license notes; • parent and trained checkpoint hashes plus complete run configurations; • external-source records and local or matched per-episode evaluations with bootstrap scripts; • generated-video manifests linking each output to its input, seed, and checkpoint; and • timing, memory, seed-variation, ablation, qualitative-selection, and failure-case reports.
blocks.zh: 复制受控比较需要: 用于渲染、支持构造、培训、采样和评价的源代码; 固定环境和依赖性版本,包括渲染器、RAFT和VAE修订; 数据分解和插图,并附有验收和许可证说明; 母站和受过训练的检查站散列并加上完整的运行配置; 外部记录以及用靴子脚本进行本地或匹配的每集评价; 生成视频表,将每项产出与其输入、种子和检查站联系起来; 以及 时间安排、内存、种子变异、断裂、质量选择和故障报告。
